name: Humanitarian funding gap
value: WFP cuts Gaza and Sudan aid; no full suspension
summary: WFP cut monthly food aid to about 900,000 displaced Sudanese and 500,000 in Gaza over funding; no full suspension found
state: WFP said on 22 Oct that funding shortages forced it to cut monthly food assistance to displaced people in Sudan, affecting about 900,000 people (Al Jazeera, 2 Nov). WFP said on 19 Oct that a shortfall would end monthly aid to 500,000 people in Gaza and shrink rations for those still reached (Khaleej Times, citing AFP). Major ration cuts meet Watch; searches on 18 Nov found no large-scale suspension of food or health aid in a famine-risk country.
for_you: Funding gaps mainly affect people relying on aid in Sudan, Gaza and other crises. UN OCHA's Financial Tracking Service publishes appeal funding levels.
rubric_hit: Watch: major ration cuts announced (WFP: ~900,000 in Sudan, 22 Oct; 500,000 in Gaza, 19 Oct); no large-scale suspension

sources.title: Al Jazeera — As aid situation worsens, displaced Sudanese worry about warnings of famine
Khaleej Times — UN World Food Programme to end monthly aid for 500,000 in Gaza

why: When appeals go unfunded, food aid and health services are cut first; funding gaps lead famine and displacement by months.
drivers: Donor budgets and aid cuts, new crises competing for funds, access constraints.

rubric.alert: Pipeline breaks forcing large-scale suspension of food or health aid in famine-risk countries.
rubric.watch: Funding more than 10 percentage points behind recent years at the same point, or major ration cuts announced.
rubric.normal: UN global appeal funding in line with recent years; no major ration cuts.
